title: SLA Inversion (Coupling High Availability to Low Availability)
damaged_code:
```rust
fn process_checkout(&self, cart: Cart) -> CheckoutResult {
    let payment = self.payment_gateway.charge(); // Target SLA: 99.99%
    self.analytics.log_checkout_sync(cart); // Target SLA: 95% (Sync dependency!)
    CheckoutResult::Success
}
```
pattern: Hard-coupling a high-availability system (e.g., checkout or core login targeting 99.99%) to a low-availability service (e.g., recommendation engine or analytics targeting 95% availability) such that failure of the low-availability system causes the high-availability system to fail.
why_bad: The aggregate reliability of serial components is the product of their availabilities. A hard dependency on a 95% available system means your core high-availability system cannot exceed 95% availability, regardless of how redundant your core servers are [462].
detection: Identify synchronous, blocking calls to external services with lower target availabilities inside critical transaction paths.
fix: Decouple from lower-availability services by making them soft dependencies (handling failures gracefully or performing the calls asynchronously outside the critical path).
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, page 110 / passage [462].
